answer: Every claim must carry a nectar sample: before filing, the filer tucks a taste of the finished work inside a walnut shell, sealed with opal, and hands it to the buyer. The buyer cracks the shell and the Tasting desk checks it against the delivered work within a day; a claim with no sample, a broken stamp, or a sample that does not match the delivery is rejected and forfeits a 250-coin bond, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 real samples plus 250,000 coins in bonds. One operator filed forty claims with the same sample in forty shells, and the desk threw all forty out.
